q: Which statement about previous study is correct for 0490?
o: Students are not expected to have studied Religious Studies before
Students must have studied it for two years
why: Cambridge does not expect learners to have studied Religious Studies before.

q: About how many guided learning hours is the syllabus designed around?
why: About 130 guided learning hours per IGCSE subject, for guidance only.

q: In which exam series can candidates be entered for 0490 according to the syllabus?
why: The syllabus says candidates can be entered in the November series.

q: Which syllabus cannot be taken with 0490 in the same series?
why: This is the named exception, along with syllabuses with the same title at the same level.

q: Who submits entries to Cambridge International?
why: Exams officers submit entries and should work with teachers.

q: What is Cambridge ICE?
o: A group award for Cambridge IGCSE
why: Cambridge ICE recognises students who pass exams in a range of subjects.

q: Can candidates retake the qualification?
o: Yes, as many times as they want
why: Candidates can retake the whole qualification as many times as they want.

q: In which language are the syllabus and assessment materials available?
why: English only.

q: What should a request for an access arrangement be based on?
o: Evidence of the candidate's barrier and their normal way of working
why: Requests must be evidence based and reflect normal working at school.

q: When should centres check which access arrangements are available?
o: At the start of the course
why: Availability should be checked at the start of the course.

q: Which is NOT a condition for approving an access arrangement?
o: It makes the exam easier for everyone
It has a reasonable cost and timeframe
It does not affect assessment security
why: Arrangements remove barriers; they do not lower the standard.

q: What does 'Ungraded' mean?
o: Performance did not meet the standard for grade G
why: Ungraded appears on the statement of results but not on the certificate.

q: Which letter on a statement of results means 'pending'?
why: Q is pending. X is no result.

q: What are the two purposes of assessment at Cambridge IGCSE?
o: To measure learning and achievement, and to show likely future success
To rank schools, and to pay teachers
To test memory only, and to punish
To compare students, and to remove them
why: These are the two purposes stated in the syllabus.

q: When will grade descriptions for 0490 be published?
o: After the first assessment of the syllabus in 2025
why: The syllabus says grade descriptions will be published after the first assessment in 2025.

q: Which new topic was added to all three religions?
why: The syllabus added Stewardship of the environment to all three religions.

q: Which new topic was added to the Islam content?
o: The five roots of Usul ad-Din
why: This topic is new for Islam.

q: Which content was removed from Judaism?
o: Simchat Torah and Shavuot festivals and knowledge of Tenakh, Mishnah and Talmud
why: These were listed as removed Judaism content.

q: Which is the best description of the 'experienced curriculum'?
o: What learners actually receive, planned and unplanned
why: It includes the outcomes of school life that are planned and unplanned.

q: What does 'spiral approach' mean?
o: Each stage returns to key ideas and builds on them
Only the hardest topics are taught
why: Learners revisit key ideas with more depth at each stage.

q: According to Cambridge, quality or quantity is more important in the curriculum?
why: Too much content leaves no time for deep understanding.

q: How are examiners asked to treat spelling and grammar in subjects that are not language tests?
o: Learners are not penalised for spelling and grammar errors
why: Examiners use positive marking.

q: What age range does Cambridge Upper Secondary cover?
why: Upper Secondary is for 14 to 16 year olds.

q: Which is part of Cambridge Advanced?
why: AS and A Level are in Cambridge Advanced.

q: Which AS or A Level subjects are named as natural next steps for strong IGCSE Religious Studies results?
why: The syllabus names Cambridge International AS and A Level Divinity and Islamic Studies.

q: What is an AS Level?
o: Half the content of an A Level
why: AS has half the content and can be taken alone or as the first half of A Level.

q: Which factor limits school timetables?
why: Staff, contracts, rooms and resources limit timetables.

q: What happens in very short lessons, according to the guide?
o: They tend to be dominated by whole-class teaching
why: Shorter periods tend to be dominated by whole-class instruction.

q: What is the zone of proximal development?
o: The area just beyond what a learner can do alone, but can do with help
The area where the teacher stands
why: Teachers scaffold learning in this zone.

q: Which is NOT a Cambridge learner attribute?
why: The five are confident, responsible, reflective, innovative and engaged.

q: What is collaborative problem solving, according to the OECD description in the guide?
o: Two or more people sharing understanding and effort to reach a solution
why: It means pooling knowledge, skills and effort.

q: How should ICT be used in the classroom?
o: To support planned teaching and learning goals, not replace them
why: Technology must enhance planned goals.

q: How long is each paper and how many marks?
why: Both papers are 1 hour 45 minutes and 80 marks.

q: How many questions do candidates answer in each paper in total?
o: Four, two from each of two chosen sections
why: They answer four questions: two in each of two sections.

q: Which topics does Paper 1 assess?
o: Worship, beliefs and scriptures, and sacred places
why: Paper 1 assesses topics 1, 2 and 3 for each religion.

q: Which topics does Paper 2 assess?
o: Festivals and fasts, rites of passage and family, and social action
why: Paper 2 assesses topics 4, 5 and 6.

q: How are the 20 marks in each question divided?
why: Part (a) 6 marks, part (b) 6 marks, part (c) 8 marks.

q: Which assessment objective is tested in part (c)?
why: Part (c) assesses evaluation.

q: What is the weighting of AO1 and AO2 in the whole qualification?
why: The syllabus states 60:40.

q: What does the command word 'Evaluate' mean?
o: Judge or calculate the quality, importance, amount or value of something
why: This is the syllabus meaning of Evaluate.

q: What does 'Identify' mean?
why: Identify means name, select or recognise.

q: What does 'Outline' mean?
why: Outline means set out the main points.

q: What should a good part (c) answer include?
o: Different points of view with evidence and a reasoned judgement
A list of facts without a conclusion
why: Part (c) needs evaluation of views, evidence and a clear judgement.

q: What should the judgement in part (c) be like?
o: Firm, clear and reasoned, building on the evidence
why: The examiner should see the position taken and the reasoning.

q: What is the best way to describe a belief in class?
o: As believers describe it, for example 'Muslims believe...'
As a fact everyone must accept
why: Teach about religion fairly and respectfully.

q: What do marks in Religious Studies reward?
o: Knowledge and reasoning, not agreement with a belief
why: AO1 and AO2 reward knowledge, evidence and reasoned evaluation.
